title: UX hunch lab notes
content:
Purpose: quick, messy scratchpad for a set of small UX-led experiments that aim to reduce token cost and perceived latency for chat-like product surfaces. Not a final PRD — think of this as the place to capture hunches, quick flows, user stories, and cheap validation paths.

Background + motivation:
- We get repeated asks for lower-cost chat modes that don't feel stripped. Teams want ways to save tokens without dramatically increasing support overhead or introducing confusing error states.
- Hypothesis: A collection of lightweight UI affordances (micro-features) can let users trade fidelity for cost in clearer, lower-friction ways than full-blown precision mode toggles.

Core ideas (short descriptions):
1) Compact Interaction Cards
   - Replace long assistant responses with tiled cards showing condensed answer + two inline expand levels: "Expand (short)" and "Expand (full)".
   - Default shows condensed to save ~40–60% tokens; expansion pulls via a targeted follow-up (cheap).
   - UX notes: show token-savings ribbon and an explicit button that says "Show full (costs tokens)".

2) Response Delta Preview
   - When model would generate >X tokens, show a one-line diff preview of what additional detail would include (like "more examples + code snippet"). User can click to get the delta.
   - Helps set expectations and avoids surprise long outputs.

3) Session Shimmer (progressive fidelity)
   - On session start, render initial replies at lower fidelity (short summaries) while warming higher fidelity shadow requests. If the user interacts with a summary, swap in higher-fidelity output.
   - Infrastructure note: requires parallel shadowing/async replacement; fallback if not available.

4) Selective Recall Toggle
   - Let user mark parts of the conversation to be recalled for later requests. Default session context is smaller; recalled segments are pinned and included.
   - Reduces average context window cost while keeping key facts.

5) Micro-Undo / Response Variants Tray
   - Instead of asking for regeneration, show 2–3 compressed variants generated in the same token budget; user can pick one, avoiding an extra regeneration roundtrip.

User stories (raw):
- As a power user, I want a concise answer quickly and can expand only if I need more, so I spend fewer tokens.
- As a developer experimenting with embedding budgets, I want predictable unit cost per reply so I can estimate monthly bills.
- As a product manager, I want to run an A/B test of "compact cards" vs. full replies to measure retention, NPS, and per-session token consumption.

Acceptance criteria / signals of success (initial):
- 20% decrease in tokens per session for users in experiment cohort without >5% drop in task completion (measured by click-to-action metric) after 4 weeks.
- Lower perceived latency (self-reported fast/slow) in followup survey for compact-card users.
- No >2% uptick in support tickets complaining about missing details.

Quick experiments (cheap to run):
- Prototype in staging with static server-side slices: show condensed text and hardcoded expansions for a small prompt set to validate user behavior (click-through to expand).
- Client-only simulation: transform full replies into compact cards on the client and track clicks/expands and subsequent user satisfaction prompts.
- Shadow parallel: run shadow high-fidelity generation for a subset of traffic to measure quality delta and time-to-ready.

Instrumentation plan (minimum viable):
- Track tokens_sent, tokens_received, expands_clicked, variant_pick_rate, followup_regens, support_ticket_tags (auto parse).
- Small UX micro-survey (1–2 question) after the first session for sample of experiment users.

Implementation notes / rough engineering impacts:
- Compact cards: mainly client + small API change to request "condensed mode" (model-level heuristics). Could also use a short-template prompt.
- Response delta preview: needs a small classification step to generate a handwritten preview label; can be an extra small classifier model or heuristic.
- Session shimmer: complex — requires either duplicate requests (costly) or a caching/warmup pipeline. Consider a limited rollout (only for select paid tiers) or a synthetic warmup (generate outline cheaply).

Guardrails and safety:
- Ensure expansions are counted clearly and shown as "may incur token costs".
- For safety-critical answers (legal/medical), default to full fidelity or require an explicit opt-in. Tag messages that should never be condensed (we'll need a simple classifier).

Open questions / unknowns (prioritized):
- Q: How do we compute "condensed" reliably across model types (LLama, Mistral, etc.)? A: try prompt templates first, then evaluate quality; consider fine-tune / distillation if needed.
- Q: Can we implement delta preview cheaply? A: run a small policy model trained on pairs (full -> delta label).
- Q: Will users find expand interactions discoverable or will it harm retention? A: A/B test with UI affordances (ribbons, microcopy).

Roadmap sketch (very rough):
- Week 0–2: client-only prototype + mock content for 3 canonical flows (FAQ, code help, product copy).
- Week 3–6: server condensed-mode toggle + instrumentation; small pilot with internal users.
- Week 7–10: A/B test public rollout (5% traffic), gather metrics.
- Week 11–16: iterate on heuristics and rollout to larger cohorts or to paid tiers.

Metrics to watch (primary + secondary):
- primary: tokens_per_active_session_delta (experiment vs control), expand_rate, conversion_to_paid (if applicable).
- secondary: average latency, NPS snippet, support ticket rates, variant_pick_rate.

Edge cases / known risks:
- Users might game compact view to avoid billing; need transparency.
- Shadowing too many requests will blow costs; cap by user tier and sample rate.
- Some content types (legal/financial) lose meaning when condensed — require classifier.

TODOs (short actionable list):
- [ ] Build client mock for compact cards (Sofia/Mika pair).
- [ ] Wire basic instrumentation (token counters + expand click). (eng: Jonah)
- [ ] Draft microcopy and billing language. (product)
- [ ] Run internal playtest with 20 employees across help, docs, and engineering.
- [ ] Create small evaluation set: 50 prompts across 5 verticals to compare condensed->expanded quality.

Notes to self:
- Keep the cadence quick; these are microfeatures that should be reversible. Aim for low cognitive overhead in UI.
- When writing prompts for condensed mode, prefer instructions like: "Summarize in 2 sentences; if examples are needed, list headline only".
- Consider saving an "expand history" so users can see what they requested expanded earlier in the session.

Last thoughts: This feels like a collection of small, testable moves rather than one big feature. Main win is product perception (faster, cheaper) with controlled rollout. Next step: pick one (compact cards) and build a client-only prototype to validate expand_rate and satisfaction within 2 weeks.

---- end of scratchpad ----
